question: Glottic carcinoma has a better prognosis than supraglottic carcinoma of equivalent T-stage because the glottis has sparse lymphatics, resulting in late nodal metastasis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The prognostic advantage of glottic carcinoma is directly linked to its sparse lymphatic supply. Supraglottic carcinoma has rich bilateral lymphatic drainage, explaining early nodal disease and worse prognosis at comparable T-stages.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Sparse glottic lymphatics mean even T2-T3 glottic carcinomas frequently present without nodal disease, which is a major contributor to the better overall prognosis. T1 glottic carcinoma treated with radiotherapy has a >90% cure rate.
